Yesterday's fleet RT average settled at **$29.62/MWh** — a meaningful step-down from the prior three-day run of $34.88–$56.20/MWh, signaling a return toward baseline conditions as the late-August heat spike dissipates. The fleet's sole RT spike node was **MV_VALV4_RN** at **$129.19/MWh**, driven by the WESLCO_HIDLBRG_1 constraint binding for 8 hours with an average shadow price of **$418.44/MWh** and a peak shadow of **$701.46/MWh at HE18** — any asset dispatching RT at that node captured exceptional locational value. **MV_VALV4_RN** posted the fleet's most negative DART at **RT exceeding DA by $12.39/MWh**, which represents **RT outperformance** for assets that held back DA commitment; its **+$69.69/MWh MCC benefit** confirms congestion directly lifted its RT settlement. On the DA-premium side, **JUNCTION_RN** led with a **DA premium of $9.09/MWh over RT**, followed by OLNEYTN_RN (+$5.78) and TOYAH_RN (+$4.91), rewarding nodes that locked in DA positions. No negative price nodes were recorded, and the absence of widespread spikes (vs. 30–32 spike nodes on 9/1–9/2) confirms the market is transitioning out of the extreme stress regime — though sustained 97–103°F temperatures across West and North Texas keep tail-risk elevated through the forecast window.

## 4. WEATHER & LOAD OUTLOOK

The 7-day forecast presents a **persistently hot, high-load environment** across all ERCOT regions — no meaningful temperature relief is in sight before mid-September. Wichita Falls leads at **103–104°F highs**, Abilene and Laredo hold **100–103°F** through September 11, and DFW sustains **100–102°F** with very low precipitation probability (<7%), pointing toward continued afternoon demand peaks well above seasonal norms. With yesterday's gross load at **85.1 GW** and solar at **30.9 GW**, load-to-solar ratios remain high during ramp events — expect continued afternoon/evening RT price spikes in HE16–HE21 as solar output rolls off and AC load persists into evening. The coastal regions (Houston at 55% precip today, Galveston 33–48% through the week) introduce some demand-side uncertainty — convective events in the Houston Ship Channel corridor could temporarily suppress load and suppress RT prices at coastal nodes like MAINLAND_RN, but this is a short-duration risk. **The bottom line for HEN:** this forecast supports a bullish RT dispatch posture through September 11, with the highest conviction at nodes exposed to West Texas and South Texas transmission corridors where sustained heat drives both load and binding constraint repeat probability.
